name: Cometas Chartularius
bio: Cometas Chartularius is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors gives no firm date for the poet. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of the Cycle of Agathias, the sixth-century anthology.
This archive carries the 2 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the third volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book IX: 586, 597).

poems.title: Book IX, 586
poems.author: Cometas Chartularius
poems.text: A, Tet me, shepherd, whose are these rows of plants? B. The olive-trees belong to Pallas and the vines round them to Dionysus. A. And whose is the corn? B. Demeter’s. A. To what gods do the flowers belong? B. To Hera and rosy Aphrodite. A. Dear Pan, stay here and ply the pipe with thy lips, for thou shalt find Echo on this sunny slope.

poems.title: Book IX, 597: In Anazarba of Cilicia
poems.author: Cometas Chartularius
poems.text: I was paralyzed from the hips to the soles of my feet, long deprived of my former activity, half-way between life and death, near to Hades, breathing only, otherwise an utter corpse. But skilled Philippus, whom you see in the picture, saved me, healing my chilling sickness; and now I, Antoninus, again tread on the earth and walk with my feet, and have feeling in every part.
